source_text:
Ὁ αὐτὸς ἠρωτήθη, ∆ιατί δέκα μέν εἰσιν αἱ νομικαὶ ἐντολαὶ, ἐννέα δὲ οἱ

μακαρισμοί; καὶ ἔφη· Ἰσάριθμος τῶν Αἰγυπτιακῶν μαστίγων ὁ ∆εκάλογος· τριπλῆς
δὲ Τριάδος εἰκὼν, ἡ τῶν μακαρισμῶν ἀρίθμησις.
ιδʹ. Ἠρωτήθη ὁ αὐτὸς, εἰ ἀρκεῖ εἷς δίκαιος δυσωπῆσαι τὸν Θεὸν, καὶ ἔφη· Ναὶ,
αὐτὸς γὰρ εἶπεν· Ἐρευνήσατε ἕνα ποιοῦντα κρῖμα καὶ δικαιοσύνην, καὶ ἵλεως ἔσομαι
παντὶ τῷ λαῷ.
ιεʹ. Ὁ αὐτὸς εἶπεν, ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς τοῖς μὲν ἁμαρτωλοῖς καὶ τὸ κεφάλαιον
παραχωρεῖ μετανοοῦσιν, ὡς τῇ πόρνῃ καὶ τῷ τελώνῃ· τοὺς δὲ δικαίους ἀπαι 65.168
τεῖ καὶ τόκους. Καὶ τοῦτό ἐστιν ὃ τοῖς ἀποστόλοις ἔλεγεν, ὅτι Ἐὰν μὴ περισσεύσῃ ἡ
δικαιοσύνη ὑμῶν, πλέον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν
βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
ις ʹ. Ἔλεγε δὲ καὶ τοῦτο, ὅτι ὀλίγον πάνυ τὰς δικαιοσύνας ὁ Θεὸς πωλεῖ τοῖς
ἀγοράζειν σπουδάζουσι· μικροῦ κλάσματος ἄρτου, εὐτελοῦς ἱματίου, ψυχροῦ
ποτηρίου, ἑνὸς ὀβολοῦ. ιζʹ. Προσετίθει δὲ καὶ τοῦτο, ὅτι παρ' ἀνθρώπῳ δανειζόμενος
ἄνθρωπος διὰ πενίαν, ἢ χρείαν εὐπορίας, καὶ ἀποδιδοὺς χάριτας μὲν ὁμολογεῖ,
κρύφα δὲ ἀποδίδωσιν αἰσχυνόμενος. Ὁ δὲ δεσπότης Θεὸς τὸ ἀνάπαλιν· κρυφῆ
δανειζόμενος ἐνώπιον ἀγγέλων καὶ ἀρχαγγέλων καὶ δικαίων ἀποδίδωσιν.
thought_title: Why ten commandments but nine beatitudes; one righteous man suffices; God sells righteousness cheaply
orientation: Epiphanius is answering questions about the number of the commandments and beatitudes, then teaching on God's mercy to sinners and his demands on the righteous.
pass_a_gloss: The same one was asked, Why are the legal commandments ten, but the beatitudes nine? And he said: Equal in number to the Egyptian scourges is the Decalogue; and an image of a triple Triad is the numbering of the beatitudes. 14. The same one was asked, whether one righteous man suffices to move God to mercy, and he said: Yes, for he himself said: Search out one doing judgment and righteousness, and I will be merciful to all the people. 15. The same one said that God to sinners even the capital forgives when they repent, as to the harlot and the tax collector; but from the righteous he demands even interest. And this is what he was saying to the apostles, that Unless your righteousness abounds more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will not enter into the kingdom of the heavens. 16. And he also said this, that for very little God sells righteousnesses to those who are eager to buy: for a small piece of bread, a cheap garment, a cold cup, one obol. 17. And he added also this, that a man borrowing from a man because of poverty, or need of resources, and repaying, acknowledges thanks openly, but in secret repays being ashamed. But the master God does the opposite: borrowing in secret, before angels and archangels and righteous ones he repays.

choices.why: Literal rendering of νομικαί as 'legal' (pertaining to the Law) and ἐντολαί as 'commandments', preserving the source's distinction from the beatitudes.

choices.english: an image of a triple Triad
choices.why: Literal: τριπλῆς Τριάδος means 'of a triple Triad' (three times three), and εἰκών is 'image'. Keeps the numerical symbolism explicit.
rejected: a figure of the threefold Trinity

choices.why: δυσωπέω means to put to shame or move by entreaty; with God as object, 'move to mercy' captures the sense of appeasing or prevailing upon him.
Literal: κεφάλαιον is the principal sum or capital of a debt, contrasted with τόκους ('interest') in the same sentence.
χάριτας is 'thanks' or 'gratitude' (accusative plural), and ὁμολογεῖ means 'acknowledges' or 'confesses'. The man openly acknowledges gratitude but repays secretly.
τὸ ἀνάπαλιν is an adverbial phrase meaning 'the reverse' or 'the opposite'. Rendered as a verb phrase to fit the English clause.

bible_refs.note: Ἐὰν μὴ περισσεύσῃ ἡ δικαιοσύνη ὑμῶν, πλέον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν

pass_b_english: The same one was asked, "Why are the legal commandments ten, but the beatitudes nine?" And he said, "The Ten Commandments are equal in number to the scourges of Egypt, and the number of the beatitudes is an image of a triple Triad."

The same one was asked whether one righteous person is enough to persuade God, and he said, "Yes, for he himself said: Search out one who does judgment and righteousness, and I will be merciful to all the people."

The same one said that God remits to sinners who repent even the principal, as with the prostitute and the tax collector, but from the righteous he demands even interest. And this is what he was saying to the apostles: Unless your righteousness abounds more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 5:20).
He also said this: God sells righteousness to those eager to buy for very little—for a small piece of bread, a cheap garment, a cold cup, one obol.

He added this too: a person who borrows from another person because of poverty or need of resources, when he repays, acknowledges thanks but repays in secret because he is ashamed. But the Lord God does the opposite: he borrows secretly but repays openly before angels and archangels and the righteous.

problems.quote: acknowledges thanks openly but repays in secret
problems.source_quote: χάριτας μὲν ὁμολογεῖ, κρύφα δὲ ἀποδίδωσιν αἰσχυνόμενος
problems.why: Greek says he confesses/acknowledges thanks but repays secretly; 'openly' is added, reversing the contrast.
problems.fix: acknowledges thanks but repays secretly, being ashamed.

problems.why: δυσωπέω means to entreat/persuade, not 'move to mercy'; the question is whether one righteous person can prevail upon God.
problems.ruling: δυσωπέω means 'to shame/embarrass into compliance' or 'prevail upon,' not 'move to mercy'; 'mercy' is imported from ἵλεως later in the verse, distorting the question's logic.

problems.quote: he borrows in secret and repays before angels
problems.source_quote: κρυφῆ δανειζόμενος ἐνώπιον ἀγγέλων καὶ ἀρχαγγέλων καὶ δικαίων ἀποδίδωσιν
problems.why: Greek says God borrows secretly but repays openly; English omits 'secretly' for borrowing, losing the contrast.
problems.fix: he borrows secretly but repays before angels and archangels and the righteous.
problems.ruling: Source 'κρυφῆ δανειζόμενος' means 'borrowing secretly'; English 'he borrows in secret' actually includes it, but contrast with 'ἐνώπιον' is clear.

edits.old: acknowledges thanks openly but repays in secret
edits.new: acknowledges thanks but repays in secret

edits.old: he borrows in secret and repays before angels
edits.new: he borrows secretly but repays before angels

fixed: Removed 'openly' from 'acknowledges thanks openly but repays in secret' because the Greek χάριτας μὲν ὁμολογεῖ, κρύφα δὲ ἀποδίδωσιν αἰσχυνόμενος contrasts acknowledgment with secret repayment, not open acknowledgment.
Changed 'move God to mercy' to 'persuade God' because δυσωπῆσαι means to entreat or persuade, not specifically to move to mercy.

Changed 'he borrows in secret and repays before angels' to 'he borrows secretly but repays before angels' to restore the contrast between secret borrowing and open repayment in the Greek κρυφῆ δανειζόμενος... ἀποδίδωσιν.

problems.quote: he borrows secretly but repays before angels and archangels and the righteous
problems.source_quote: κρυφῆ δανειζόμενος ἐνώπιον ἀγγέλων καὶ ἀρχαγγέλων καὶ δικαίων ἀποδίδωσιν
problems.why: Source says God repays secretly, not borrows secretly; ἀνάπαλιν reverses both actions
problems.fix: he lends secretly but repays openly before angels and archangels and the righteous
problems.ruling: κρυφῇ modifies δανιζόμενος (borrows secretly); ἀνάπαλιν reverses both: borrows secretly, repays openly.

edits.old: he borrows secretly but repays before angels and archangels and the righteous
edits.new: he lends secretly but repays openly before angels and archangels and the righteous

fixed: Source: κρυφῆ δανειζόμενος ἐνώπιον ἀγγέλων καὶ ἀρχαγγέλων καὶ δικαίων ἀποδίδωσιν. The participle δανειζόμενος is middle/passive of δανείζω, which in the middle means 'to lend' (borrow is δανείζομαι in the active sense of taking a loan, but here the context of God as master and the contrast with the human borrower makes 'lend' correct). The adverb κρυφῆ modifies the lending, and ἀποδίδωσιν ('repays') is contrasted with the human's secret repayment, so God repays openly (ἐνώπιον). The English 'borrows secretly' misstates the source; changed to 'lends secretly but repays openly'.

problems.quote: he lends secretly but repays openly
problems.source_quote: κρυφῆ δανειζόμενος ἐνώπιον ἀγγέλων καὶ ἀρχαγγέλων καὶ δικαίων ἀποδίδωσιν
problems.why: ἀνάπαλιν refers to God borrowing secretly but repaying openly, not lending secretly; the subject of δανειζόμενος is God
problems.fix: he borrows secretly but repays openly before angels and archangels and the righteous

problems.quote: God forgives sinners who repent even the capital
problems.source_quote: ὁ Θεὸς τοῖς μὲν ἁμαρτωλοῖς καὶ τὸ κεφάλαιον παραχωρεῖ μετανοοῦσιν
problems.why: τὸ κεφάλαιον means 'the principal' (debt), not 'capital' (punishment); παραχωρεῖ means 'remits/lets go', not 'forgives'
problems.fix: God remits to sinners who repent even the principal, as with the prostitute and the tax collector
problems.ruling: τὸ κεφάλαιον = 'principal' (debt), not 'capital' (punishment); context is interest/loans, so meaning is changed.

edits.old: he lends secretly but repays openly
edits.new: he borrows secretly but repays openly

edits.old: God forgives sinners who repent even the capital
edits.new: God remits to sinners who repent even the principal

fixed: Changed 'lends' to 'borrows' because δανειζόμενος is middle/passive and means borrowing, not lending; the subject is God.
Changed 'forgives...the capital' to 'remits...the principal' because κεφάλαιον means principal (debt), not capital punishment, and παραχωρεῖ means remits/lets go.

refereed.quote: he borrows secretly but repays openly
refereed.source_quote: κρυφῆ δανειζόμενος ἐνώπιον ἀγγέλων καὶ ἀρχαγγέλων καὶ δικαίων ἀποδίδωσιν
refereed.why: ἀποδίδωσιν lacks 'openly'; God repays before angels etc., not 'openly' as contrast.
refereed.fix: he borrows secretly but repays before angels and archangels and the righteous
refereed.ruling: ἐνώπιον means 'before/in the presence of', not 'openly'; God repays before angels, not openly as contrast.
